title: Model Serving and API Compatibility Contracts
summary: A runnable Windows x64 CPU lab supplement for the existing Model Serving and API Compatibility Contracts lesson. In one PowerShell 7.6+ session, learners capture an absolute repository root, verify pinned llama.cpp and Qwen artifacts, run an ownership-checked loopback service, collect synthetic and live conformance evidence, and preserve secret continuity across each owned lifecycle. They diagnose a protected SSE failure, compare fictional offline adapters with correct 7, 5, 12, 17, and 25-test accounting, test their own ChangedAdapter through unchanged protected tests before viewing the answer, and rehearse changed-port recovery with ConnectionRefused as the only accepted proof of old-port closure. The qualified environment was PowerShell 7.6.6, .NET 10.0.12, and Python 3.13.9. The code is intended for Python 3.11+, but other versions are not claimed as qualified. The qualifying v3 live receipt has nine observed live checks and three not-observed checks; a new run must report client_timeout honestly if a response beats the 50 millisecond deadline. The lab does not certify production security, full OpenAI compatibility, server-side cancellation, gateway rate limiting, or sustained capacity.
objectives: Separate the model runtime, inference server, gateway, application adapter, and public endpoint trust boundaries.
Define liveness, readiness, model identity, inference, streaming, cancellation, timeout, error, and overload contracts.
Treat OpenAI-compatible and other compatibility claims as tested subsets rather than universal equivalence.
Publish a versioned conformance suite and migration boundary that preserves application behavior across runtimes.

sections.title: Separate runtime, server, gateway, and application contracts
paragraphs: The model runtime loads and executes the artifact. An inference server turns runtime operations into a network protocol. A gateway can enforce identity, authorization, limits, routing, policy, audit, and stable external names. An application adapter maps product-owned requests and outcomes to the selected serving protocol. Keep these layers explicit so a runtime replacement does not silently rewrite policy or learner-facing behavior.

Bind the served model name to the immutable model and runtime bundle behind it. A friendly alias can support controlled replacement, but responses, telemetry, evaluation, and rollback evidence must retain the exact underlying identity.

sections.title: Define liveness, readiness, and model identity separately
paragraphs: Liveness asks whether the server process can respond and should not require every downstream dependency to be healthy. Readiness asks whether this instance should receive inference traffic. Model readiness confirms that the intended model and version are loaded and able to serve. Model metadata should identify the served contract without exposing secrets, internal paths, or unnecessary infrastructure details.

KServe's Open Inference Protocol V2 defines distinct server liveness, server readiness, model readiness, model metadata, and inference endpoints. Whether using that protocol or another, test transition behavior during startup, load, unload, pressure, failed dependencies, update, and rollback. A process that returns HTTP 200 while the wrong model is loaded is not ready.

sections.title: Own the inference and failure contract
paragraphs: Version the allowed request fields, roles or input parts, modalities, encoding, context and output limits, sampling controls, stop rules, tools if any, response schema, model identity, usage accounting, finish reasons, safety or policy outcomes, and extension fields. Reject unsupported or ambiguous inputs instead of silently ignoring them.

Define authentication and authorization outside model prompts. Specify request identifiers, idempotency expectations, maximum body size, timeouts, cancellation, streaming event order, disconnect behavior, queue and rate limits, overload responses, retryability, error codes, observability identifiers, and redaction. Bound retries so one overloaded request does not multiply load.

sections.title: Treat compatibility as a tested subset
paragraphs: An OpenAI-compatible server may implement selected paths and fields while differing in model discovery, roles, tools, structured output, streaming chunks, token accounting, errors, limits, extensions, or unsupported parameters. vLLM documents an OpenAI-compatible server, but application compatibility still depends on the exact version, endpoint, model, configuration, and features used.

Write a conformance matrix for the application-owned subset. Include positive, boundary, invalid, unauthorized, overloaded, timeout, cancellation, streaming, and restart cases. Record required, transformed, ignored, emulated, rejected, and unavailable behavior. Never infer full protocol or behavioral equivalence from one successful chat request.
sections.callout: Compatible with a named subset is testable. Drop-in replacement without a versioned suite is an assumption.

sections.title: Preserve a portable adapter and reversible cutover
paragraphs: Keep user outcomes, application schemas, authorization policy, evaluation cases, trace fields, postconditions, error categories, and recovery rules above the runtime adapter. Put protocol-specific field names, streaming events, tool formats, and server extensions behind the adapter. Avoid a lowest-common-denominator contract that hides capabilities or safety differences.

For a runtime change, run the same conformance and evaluation suites against baseline and candidate, compare performance and failure behavior, canary a bounded route, preserve exact telemetry, and retain the last verified adapter and serving bundle. Roll back on critical contract, quality, security, latency, capacity, or observability regression.

sections.title: Run a pinned CPU service and collect one cohesive baseline
paragraphs: Start from the root of the cloned content repository and continue in the same PowerShell session for all six sections. The first command captures that root as an absolute path before changing directory. The supplied scripts and tests are canonical assets under modules/self-hosted-model-operations/lab/serving-contract/. The repository does not contain the model or runtime binaries. This qualified lab requires Windows x64 and PowerShell 7.6 or newer. It was tested with PowerShell 7.6.6, .NET 10.0.12, and a normal Python 3.13.9 installation exposing the python command. The Python code is intended for Python 3.11 or newer, but only Python 3.13.9 is qualified by the supplied evidence. Start-ServingLab.ps1 also requires Invoke-ServingChild.ps1 and Serving-Time.ps1 in the same folder, so the command checks all required files before setup.

The pinned runtime archive is llama-b10964-bin-win-cpu-x64.zip, exactly 18427629 bytes, with SHA-256 917f39c076402c421224824607397af20f53625a60defc20e8dd22446bf4c5d7 and commit b29c606e28a01b1bc8c1351026a0fa6e616bf6c4. The pinned model is Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf, exactly 639446688 bytes, with SHA-256 9465e63a22add5354d9bb4b99e90117043c7124007664907259bd16d043bb031 and revision 23749fefcc72300e3a2ad315e1317431b06b590a. Their exact sum is 657874317 bytes, roughly 658 MB, before HTTPS overhead, extracted runtime DLLs, logs, and receipts. Peak disk use, memory use, startup duration, and inference duration are UNKNOWN until measured on the learner's computer. Plan for a long-running CPU exercise rather than treating the 190-minute lesson estimate as a machine-performance guarantee.

Choose a new run directory below the learner-controlled lab-runs directory. The command creates its parent explicitly, refuses to reuse the run directory or workspace, and keeps staging below the workspace rather than using the system temporary directory. Setup verifies the archive and model pins plus the complete extracted runtime tree. To use the supported read-only cache path, replace the setup command with the commented ArtifactCache form. Cached and copied files must still pass all pinned checks.

The server binds only to 127.0.0.1 and uses two CPU threads, context size 2048, zero GPU layers, parallelism one, no web UI, and alias p42-qwen3-06b. The command generates one secret with RandomNumberGenerator.Create(), places it only in the current PowerShell environment, starts the server, tests missing-key rejection separately, runs the live client with that same key, and stops the owned server before clearing the key. Start passes the value to the child as LLAMA_API_KEY. Stop checks the recorded PID, executable path, and process-start instant, using the implementation's comparison tolerance, before acting.

The eight test_conformance.py tests are synthetic HTTP-fixture tests. They establish client behavior, not live inference. The subsequent conformance.py invocation produces live runtime evidence. Native Python exit codes are checked, the receipt is reserved as a new path, and cleanup remains ownership checked even after a client failure. A successful run does not establish TLS, gateway rate limiting, multiuser authorization, production auditing, full protocol compatibility, sustained capacity, or server-side cancellation.

code.label: PowerShell preflight, setup, synthetic tests, owned live run, and cleanup

sections.title: Classify live, lifecycle, and unverified evidence separately
paragraphs: Continue in the same PowerShell session so $repoRoot, $workspace, $evidence, and $receipt still identify the baseline created in the preceding section. This block returns to the lab through the saved absolute repository root rather than resolving a relative path from the current directory. The verified receipt schema contains 12 checks in total. The supplied qualifying receipt records nine named live observations: health_public, authentication_rejection, server_identity, bounded_completion, stream, early_disconnect, recovery_after_disconnect, client_timeout, and overload_observation. It records server_side_cancellation, stop_restart_recovery, and artifact_hashes as not-observed in that port-only receipt. Read the actual receipt rather than treating a prior qualifying run as evidence for a new run.

Public /health returning HTTP 200 is readiness evidence, not authentication evidence. The baseline command separately tests a missing key, while conformance tests a wrong key. Authenticated /v1/models must contain p42-qwen3-06b. The alias is useful identity evidence but is not cryptographic proof of the artifacts. Setup records establish byte counts, hashes, and full-tree verification. Start and Stop evidence establish process and listener ownership. Those facts are separate evidence streams and are not fields proven by the port-only conformance receipt.

A bounded completion must contain generated text, but its exact text is nondeterministic. Streaming must assemble SSE records independently of network chunk boundaries, contain generated text, and finish with [DONE]. Early disconnect establishes client closure, and the following recovery request establishes that the service answered again. The deliberate 50 millisecond client-timeout experiment establishes timeout classification only if the socket deadline expires. On some machines a reply can arrive first. In that case, client_timeout being not-observed is honest, but it leaves a required learner experiment unmet. It is not a universal server failure and it does not prove server cancellation. The stream retains a separate 30-second total deadline. These budgets are lab qualification settings, not availability promises or service-level objectives.

The supplied qualifying receipt's overload sample reported four HTTP 200 outcomes. That is an observation from one run, not proof of queueing, capacity, contention, rate limiting, or sustained capacity. Server-side cancellation remains not-observed because this client has no server-owned cancellation telemetry. Stop and restart recovery, and the artifact hashes, are separate evidence even though the receipt has not-observed placeholders for them. If cancellation, TLS, gateway rate limiting, multiuser security, or production auditing is required, record it as unavailable or not-observed and block deployment until an appropriate implementation and direct evidence exist.

Run the independent lifecycle script while the baseline server remains stopped. The block creates a fresh secret and holds that same key for both server cycles owned by Test-ServingLifecycle.ps1. It does not start another baseline server. The script checks four meaningful negative cases: preserving a foreign directory, rejecting a changed runtime ZIP, refusing an occupied port, and refusing forged process state. It also performs an ownership-checked start, authenticated identity check, stop, restart with the same key, identity recovery, and final stop. The key is cleared only after the entire lifecycle test completes. Its evidence belongs beside the live receipt rather than inside it. The learner gate requires the eight observations other than client_timeout. It separately accepts client_timeout only when observed; a failed or not-observed timeout is recorded and causes this section to fail as an unmet experiment.

code.label: PowerShell receipt review and independent lifecycle evidence

sections.title: Diagnose a streaming contract failure and restore fail-closed parsing
paragraphs: Continue in the same PowerShell session and use the saved absolute repository root. Diagnose failures by their causes rather than changing labels. A size or hash mismatch means the bytes are not the pinned artifact, even when the filename matches. Preserve the failed workspace and create a new workspace from the exact artifact. A full-tree mismatch means an executable, DLL, or other extracted file is missing, changed, or extra. Copying only llama-server.exe is not a repair. An occupied port belongs to another process until ownership evidence says otherwise. A stop refusal protects an unmatched PID, path, or recorded start instant and must never be bypassed with a process-name kill.

Protocol evidence has similarly narrow meanings. Public health cannot substitute for rejection on authenticated endpoints. Nonempty streamed text cannot substitute for a terminal [DONE] event. A socket read is not an SSE record, so a correct parser buffers incomplete data and rejects truncated records, malformed choices, duplicate termination, data after termination, and a stream ending without termination. A client timeout says only that the client stopped waiting. Direct server-side cancellation would require server-owned telemetry or another direct server observation not supplied by this lab.

The worked exercise creates an isolated practice directory, copies conformance.py and the unchanged protected test_conformance.py into it, and creates an exclusive reference backup. It removes exactly the final missing-DONE guard from only the copied module. The complete protected suite must then return a nonzero exit code. The command extracts the concrete failing protected test identifier and runs that named test alone, again requiring nonzero. This avoids guessing a test class or method name while ensuring unittest imports the mutated conformance.py from the practice directory.

Restore the copied module from its untouched reference backup and rerun all eight protected tests. The suite must return zero after restoration. The canonical client outside the practice directory is never edited or overwritten. The causal lesson is that without the guard, a truncated stream can be accepted as complete. Recovery therefore means restoring fail-closed parsing, rerunning protected tests, and using only the canonical client for a new live receipt.

When a result is unavailable or not-observed, record why and what would establish it. For example, server-side cancellation needs direct server telemetry correlated to the disconnected request. A body-size contract needs explicit boundary and over-limit requests with expected status and bounded error bodies. Do not convert absence of evidence into PASS, and do not claim failure merely because a check was not attempted.

code.label: PowerShell isolated missing-DONE mutation and protected recovery

sections.title: Compare two fictional adapters with a completed offline matrix
paragraphs: Continue in the same PowerShell session and return through $repoRoot. This exercise is offline and synthetic. Adapter A and Adapter B are hypothetical mappings, not two actual model providers, servers, or model runtimes. Their fixed responses, identities, latency values, error values, and gate decisions are classroom fixtures. The adapter test suites and six-line executable output cannot qualify the separate llama.cpp and Qwen runtime.

The application-owned request and normalized response have four original fields. requestId is a required nonempty string echoed exactly. category is required and must be billing, technical, account_recovery, or access. explanation must remain nonempty after trimming. modelArtifactId is required, echoed, and verified exactly. Adapter A maps these to ticket_id, kind, reason, and artifact. Adapter B maps them to id, label, description, and model_id, with the declared transformation of trimming description.

The completed six-row matrix appears in the runnable block. Required means omission or mismatch is a contract failure. Transformed means the representation changes under an explicit tested rule. Rejected means the adapter refuses the request. Unavailable means the capability is not provided and must produce an error rather than being silently discarded. The original contract rejects tools and does not provide confidential handling.

The gate rejects incomplete or duplicate fixture coverage, malformed normalized output, identity or artifact mismatch, Boolean metrics, missing metrics, negative or nonfinite values, numeric overflow, a canary above 0.10, increased candidate errors, and candidate latency above 1.5 times baseline. Exact synthetic metric and immutable-style identity values must be read from the supplied local fixture code and preserved in the generated exercise evidence. They are not operational measurements and must not be replaced with guessed values.

Run the seven original adapter tests in test_adapter_exercise.py, the five rollback-boundary tests in test_adapter_rollback_boundaries.py, and the combined 12-test original regression. Then run the five changed-contract tests separately and all three adapter files as a 17-test combined regression. Finally run test_conformance.py's eight tests and all four files as a 25-test regression. The test counts are checked from unittest output so a renamed, missing, or unexpectedly added test does not silently change the claimed scope. Finally run the executable and require exactly six lines: MATRIX_ROWS=6, FIXTURES=3 ADAPTER_RUNS=6 PASS, FLAWED_CANDIDATE=HOLD, CORRECTED_CANDIDATE=OFFLINE_ELIGIBLE, ROLLBACK=OFFLINE_ELIGIBLE RERUN=3, and the deploymentAuthorization false JSON line. HOLD is causal because BrokenCandidate erases the required explanation. The corrected verdict remains only OFFLINE_ELIGIBLE. Rollback actually restores Adapter A and reruns all three original fixtures.

code.label: PowerShell completed matrix, 25-test regression accounting, and exact offline output
code.code:
Set-Location (Join-Path $repoRoot 'modules/self-hosted-model-operations/lab/serving-contract')

$matrix = @'
APPLICATION FIELD | APPLICATION CONTRACT       | ADAPTER A                 | ADAPTER B
requestId        | required, exact echo         | ticket_id, required exact | id, required exact
category         | required, exact allowed value| kind, required exact      | label, required exact
explanation      | required, nonempty           | reason, required nonempty | description, transformed by trim
modelArtifactId  | required, exact and verified | artifact, verified exact  | model_id, verified exact
tools            | rejected as unsupported      | rejected                  | unavailable, error
confidential     | unavailable in original      | rejected                  | unavailable, error
'@
Write-Host $matrix

function Invoke-CountedUnittest {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][int]$ExpectedCount,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string[]]$TestFiles,
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Label
    )
    $testOutput = & python -m unittest -v @TestFiles 2>&1
    $testExit = $LASTEXITCODE
    $testOutput | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }
    if ($testExit -ne 0) {
        throw "$Label failed with exit code $testExit"
    }
    $joinedOutput = $testOutput -join "`n"
    $runMatch = [regex]::Match($joinedOutput, '(?m)^Ran (\d+) tests? in ')
    if (-not $runMatch.Success -or [int]$runMatch.Groups[1].Value -ne $ExpectedCount) {
        throw "$Label did not run the expected $ExpectedCount tests."
    }
}

Invoke-CountedUnittest -ExpectedCount 7 -TestFiles @('test_adapter_exercise.py') -Label 'Original adapter suite'
Invoke-CountedUnittest -ExpectedCount 5 -TestFiles @('test_adapter_rollback_boundaries.py') -Label 'Rollback-boundary suite'
Invoke-CountedUnittest -ExpectedCount 12 -TestFiles @('test_adapter_exercise.py', 'test_adapter_rollback_boundaries.py') -Label 'Original plus rollback regression'
Invoke-CountedUnittest -ExpectedCount 5 -TestFiles @('test_adapter_changed.py') -Label 'Changed-contract reference suite'
Invoke-CountedUnittest -ExpectedCount 17 -TestFiles @('test_adapter_exercise.py', 'test_adapter_changed.py', 'test_adapter_rollback_boundaries.py') -Label 'Combined adapter regression'
Invoke-CountedUnittest -ExpectedCount 8 -TestFiles @('test_conformance.py') -Label 'Conformance suite'
Invoke-CountedUnittest -ExpectedCount 25 -TestFiles @('test_adapter_exercise.py', 'test_adapter_changed.py', 'test_adapter_rollback_boundaries.py', 'test_conformance.py') -Label 'All supplied test regression'

$output = & python adapter_exercise.py
$programExit = $LASTEXITCODE
$output | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }
if ($programExit -ne 0) {
    throw "adapter_exercise.py failed with exit code $programExit"
}
$expected = @(
    'MATRIX_ROWS=6',
    'FIXTURES=3 ADAPTER_RUNS=6 PASS',
    'FLAWED_CANDIDATE=HOLD',
    'CORRECTED_CANDIDATE=OFFLINE_ELIGIBLE',
    'ROLLBACK=OFFLINE_ELIGIBLE RERUN=3',
    '{"deploymentAuthorization": false, "scope": "offline synthetic fictional adapters"}'
)
if (@($output).Count -ne 6 -or (Compare-Object -ReferenceObject $expected -DifferenceObject @($output) -SyncWindow 0)) {
    throw 'The offline executable did not produce the documented six exact lines.'
}

sections.title: Practice the changed confidential-recovery contract before reading the answer
paragraphs: Continue in the same PowerShell session and return through $repoRoot. The changed requirement adds confidential account-recovery escalation without removing any original behavior. When present, confidential must be an actual Boolean. Integer 1 is invalid even though Python normally treats bool as an integer subclass. A true value is permitted only when the application category is account_recovery. The transport request and response carry confidential, and their label must become exactly confidential_account_recovery. The normalized application response still has exactly four fields. It does not contain a confidential flag. Its category is confidential_account_recovery, which conveys the escalation.

Unknown fields, a caller directly supplying the escalated category, wrong request identity, wrong artifact identity, and a missing escalation must fail explicitly. Original four-field requests must continue to pass unchanged. The unchanged protected tests include 15 negative changed-contract cases and checks for original behavior preservation. Accepting confidential while retaining an ordinary recovery label would lose a consequential routing distinction even if the transport returned success.

Work in a new practice directory and implement class ChangedAdapter in learner_changed_adapter.py before opening adapter_answer.py. The learner class must provide map_request(request) and normalize_response(transport, request), preserve the original Adapter B behavior, enforce the changed contract, and return the normalized four-field response. The harness loads learner_changed_adapter.ChangedAdapter, assigns that class to adapter_answer.ChangedAdapter, and only then imports the unchanged protected test_adapter_changed module. Helper fixtures may still come from adapter_answer, but the protected tests execute the learner's class. The learner may edit and rerun the harness until all five protected test methods pass. Nonzero failures remain visible and must not be replaced by self-recorded cases.

Before the learner attempt, the command runs the exact protected method test_original_fails_changed_requirement against the original adapter. That unittest is expected to report OK because it passes by asserting that original Adapter B raises ContractError. It does not mean the original adapter satisfies the changed requirement. After the learner attempt has actually been tested, the command copies and displays the reference answer, runs the five-test reference suite, and then runs the complete 17-test adapter regression across the seven original tests, five changed tests, and five rollback-boundary tests. No unittest expectation is edited.

Causal grading should identify why each guard exists. Erasing explanation loses a required user-visible result. Accepting confidential without escalation loses routing meaning. Failing to verify modelArtifactId can associate output with the wrong artifact. Permitting direct use of the transport-only category lets callers bypass application validation. These are contract failures, not cosmetic field-name differences. The passing learner or reference answer remains offline unit evidence and is not deployment authorization.

class ChangedAdapter(AdapterB):

    $harness = @'

import adapter_answer
from learner_changed_adapter import ChangedAdapter as LearnerChangedAdapter

# Keep supplied fixture helpers, but bind the unchanged protected tests to the learner class.

import test_adapter_changed

'@
    Set-Content -LiteralPath .\run_learner_changed_tests.py -Value $harness -Encoding utf8 -NoNewline

    Write-Host 'Implement class ChangedAdapter with map_request and normalize_response in learner_changed_adapter.py.'
    Write-Host 'The normalized result has exactly requestId, category, explanation, and modelArtifactId; escalation is represented by category.'
    notepad.exe $learnerFile
    Read-Host 'After saving the learner implementation, press Enter to run the unchanged protected tests'

    python .\run_learner_changed_tests.py
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw 'The learner ChangedAdapter failed unchanged protected tests. Edit learner_changed_adapter.py and rerun .\run_learner_changed_tests.py until it passes before inspecting the answer.'
    }

    Write-Host 'Learner implementation passed the unchanged protected changed-contract tests. Reference answer follows.'
    Get-Content -LiteralPath .\adapter_answer.py

    python -m unittest -v test_adapter_changed.py
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "The supplied changed-contract answer tests failed with exit code $LASTEXITCODE"
    }

    $regressionOutput = & python -m unittest -v test_adapter_exercise.py test_adapter_changed.py test_adapter_rollback_boundaries.py 2>&1
    $regressionExit = $LASTEXITCODE
    $regressionOutput | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }
    if ($regressionExit -ne 0) {
        throw "The combined adapter regression failed with exit code $regressionExit"
    }
    $regressionText = $regressionOutput -join "`n"
    $regressionMatch = [regex]::Match($regressionText, '(?m)^Ran (\d+) tests? in ')
    if (-not $regressionMatch.Success -or [int]$regressionMatch.Groups[1].Value -ne 17) {
        throw 'The combined adapter regression did not run the expected 17 tests.'
    }
} finally {
    Pop-Location
}
Write-Host "Learner implementation preserved at: $learnerFile"

sections.title: Rehearse owned changed-port recovery, cutover, and rollback
paragraphs: Continue in the same PowerShell session and use $repoRoot to identify the same baseline run directory. This task changes only the serving port from 11842 to 11901. If server-state.json exists, it invokes the ownership-checked Stop script before creating a new key. If no state exists because the baseline already stopped, it does not call Stop unconditionally. It then proves that the old port is closed only when a bounded connection attempt ends with SocketError.ConnectionRefused.

The old-port check treats a successful connection as failure. ConnectAsync.Wait(1000) can throw AggregateException when the connection task faults, so the command unwraps only a SocketException whose SocketErrorCode is ConnectionRefused as proof of closure. A one-second wait that does not complete, cancellation, or any other network error is not proof that the port is closed and causes the rehearsal to fail. The TcpClient is disposed in all cases, and the command does not swallow its own successful-connection assertion.

The expected causal change is narrow. The listener and client URL move to 127.0.0.1:11901. The model hash, runtime hash, alias, authentication source, context size, CPU thread count, GPU-layer count, and parallelism do not change. Setup evidence remains the source for artifact hashes. Start and Stop evidence remain the source for recorded PID, path, start instant, listener ownership, and restart. The new port-only receipt remains the source for endpoint behavior.

The command generates a new secret because it creates a new server lifecycle. Start and conformance use that same key. The fresh receipt path must not exist. In the nested finally blocks, Stop runs while the key is still present and before the environment value and byte array are cleared. The changed receipt must contain the same nine named live checks. Eight are required observations. client_timeout is also a required experiment, but a fast reply can make it honestly not-observed. The command records that state and fails the learner gate without declaring a universal server failure. Generated text and overload outcomes can vary. Server-side cancellation remains not-observed unless direct server telemetry is added.

A complete operational rehearsal combines separate evidence: setup pins and full-tree verification, ownership-checked old-port stop, old-port connection refusal, owned new-port start, authenticated alias, fresh bounded and streamed inference, recovery after disconnect, timeout experiment, and final ownership-checked stop. Apply the original cutover and rollback rule above this local exercise. Compare baseline and candidate with the same conformance, invalid-input, body-limit, stream-truncation, timeout, restart, recovery, quality, safety, latency, capacity, and observability cases. Preserve exact identities and a bounded canary. Fail closed on critical authentication, identity, content, streaming, safety, or evidence regressions. Retain the prior verified adapter and serving bundle, and perform rollback through ownership-checked stop and restart rather than process-name termination.

activity.title: Design a portable serving conformance suite
instructions: Define synthetic liveness, readiness, model-readiness, identity, inference, streaming, cancellation, timeout, invalid-input, unauthorized, rate-limit, and overload contracts. Distinguish public health from authenticated checks, client timeout from server cancellation, and observed, failed, unavailable, and not-observed evidence.

Use Windows x64 and PowerShell 7.6 or newer, and continue in the same PowerShell session across all six commands. Capture the repository root as an absolute path before the first Set-Location. The qualified environment is PowerShell 7.6.6, .NET 10.0.12, and a normal Python 3.13.9 installation exposing python. Treat Python 3.11 or newer as intended compatibility, not as qualified beyond 3.13.9 without additional evidence.

Run the supplied pinned CPU service from modules/self-hosted-model-operations/lab/serving-contract/ in a new absolute workspace under a learner-controlled lab-runs directory. Preserve the exact runtime and model filenames, revisions, byte counts, SHA-256 values, complete extracted-tree verification, process and listener ownership evidence, alias, and unique lifecycle records. Use the optional ArtifactCache only as a read-only source whose files still pass all pins.

Run the eight synthetic test_conformance.py tests separately from live model-runtime conformance. For the live baseline, test missing-key rejection separately, retain the client's wrong-key test, use only fictional nonsensitive messages, require a new receipt path, and check native Python exit codes. Treat an ordinary 30-second budget as a proposed qualification budget rather than a guarantee, while preserving the deliberate 50 millisecond timeout and 30-second streaming deadline.

Record the nine named live checks: public health, authentication rejection, authenticated identity, bounded nonempty completion, SSE reconstruction with terminal [DONE], early disconnect, post-disconnect recovery, client timeout, and overload observation. If a response beats the 50 millisecond timeout, record client_timeout as not-observed and the experiment as unmet rather than asserting universal server failure. Keep server-side cancellation not-observed without server-owned telemetry. Keep setup hashes, full-tree verification, and ownership-checked stop or restart evidence separate from the port-only receipt.

Diagnose pinned-size, hash, full-tree, occupied-port, readiness, authentication, SSE truncation, timeout, overload, and stop-ownership failures causally. Complete the isolated missing-DONE mutation with the exact supplied mutator, require a protected-test failure, restore from the exclusive backup, and require all eight protected tests to pass without editing the canonical client.

Choose the original application-owned four-field request and normalized response schema and map it to the two hypothetical fictional adapters. Run the seven original tests in test_adapter_exercise.py, five rollback-boundary tests in test_adapter_rollback_boundaries.py, their 12-test regression, five changed tests, and the combined 17-test adapter regression. Run the eight test_conformance.py tests separately and the all-four-file regression as 25 tests. Also require the exact six-line executable output, flawed-candidate HOLD decision, corrected OFFLINE_ELIGIBLE decision, and actual three-case rollback. State that this does not observe two real providers or authorize deployment.

Use the completed six-row matrix: requestId is required and maps to ticket_id for A and id for B; category is required exact and maps to kind and label; explanation is required nonempty and maps to reason while B transforms it by trimming into description; modelArtifactId is required and verified through artifact and model_id; tools are rejected by A and unavailable with an error in B; confidential is unavailable in the original contract, rejected by A, and unavailable with an error in B.

Write deterministic normal, boundary, invalid-input, unauthorized, body-limit, wrong-identity, malformed-error, timeout, overload, restart, recovery, and stream-truncation cases with expected status, bounded body, event order, identity, and telemetry. Include missing, duplicate, and post-terminal SSE events. If the supplied runnable client does not implement a case, keep it as an explicit unverified gate rather than inventing a result.

Complete the confidential account-recovery task before reading the displayed reference answer. Explain that test_original_fails_changed_requirement passes by asserting the original adapter rejects the new requirement. Implement learner_changed_adapter.ChangedAdapter with map_request and normalize_response, then use the supplied harness to bind it into adapter_answer before importing and running the unchanged protected tests. Require the learner to pass preservation checks and 15 negative changed cases. Verify that confidential is an actual Boolean, true is valid only for account_recovery, transport carries the flag and confidential_account_recovery label, and the normalized response has exactly four fields with escalation represented by category.

Design a baseline-candidate cutover and rollback that fails closed on critical contract, quality, safety, authentication, identity, latency, capacity, or observability regression. Use the same conformance and evaluation suites, exact model and runtime identities, a bounded canary, explicit stop conditions, and retained prior artifacts. Rehearse ownership-checked stop on 11842, require SocketError.ConnectionRefused as the only proof of old-port closure, start the owned service on 11901, create a new receipt, check identity and recovery, and perform a final owned stop.
evidence: A versioned endpoint and error contract separating public liveness, readiness, model identity, authenticated inference, invalid input, body limits, streaming, timeout, cancellation, unauthorized access, overload, restart, and recovery semantics.

Runtime qualification evidence stating PowerShell 7.6+ is required and identifying PowerShell 7.6.6, .NET 10.0.12, and Python 3.13.9 as the tested versions. Any claim that another Python 3.11+ version works requires a new qualification run.

Setup evidence with runtime asset llama-b10964-bin-win-cpu-x64.zip at commit b29c606e28a01b1bc8c1351026a0fa6e616bf6c4, bytes 18427629, and SHA-256 917f39c076402c421224824607397af20f53625a60defc20e8dd22446bf4c5d7; model Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf at revision 23749fefcc72300e3a2ad315e1317431b06b590a, bytes 639446688, and SHA-256 9465e63a22add5354d9bb4b99e90117043c7124007664907259bd16d043bb031; full extracted-tree verification; and preserved staging evidence.

Lifecycle evidence containing the recorded PID, executable path, start instant, port, and alias; listener ownership checks; four negative lifecycle checks; one secret held across the lifecycle test's two owned cycles; ownership-checked stop and restart records; and unique redacted logs without a secret.

Eight passing synthetic client unit tests kept separate from a live receipt whose 12 checks are individually labeled observed, failed, or not-observed. The qualifying receipt has nine named observations and not-observed entries for server-side cancellation, stop_restart_recovery, and artifact_hashes. Missing-key evidence is separate from the wrong-key receipt check, and setup or lifecycle evidence is not represented as if the port-only client generated it.

An explicit limitation record stating that a client_timeout result can be not-observed when a reply arrives before 50 milliseconds, leaving the learner experiment unmet without proving universal server failure. Also state that server-side cancellation is not-observed and that TLS, gateway rate limiting, multiuser authorization, production auditing, full OpenAI compatibility, and sustained capacity are not implemented or established.

A protected streaming-parser mutation record showing a nonzero test result when the missing-DONE guard is removed, the concrete named protected test that detected it, restoration from the reference copy, and a zero exit from the complete eight-test suite.

A completed two-adapter matrix and deterministic fixture set covering required, transformed, rejected, and unavailable behavior, plus results for seven original tests, five rollback-boundary tests, the 12-test original regression, five changed tests, the 17-test combined adapter regression, eight conformance tests, and the 25-test all-four-file regression. Include the six exact executable output lines. Synthetic fixture latency, error, canary, model-artifact, and bundle-identity values must be copied from the supplied fixture code, labeled synthetic, and never reported as live measurements.

A changed-contract record containing the learner's task-first ChangedAdapter implementation, the harness that binds it before importing unchanged protected tests, a passing five-method protected run that includes original preservation and 15 negative changed cases, the expected original-adapter rejection, the later reference-answer run, and causal feedback for Boolean validation, escalation, explanation, request identity, and artifact identity. Record that the normalized changed response has four fields and conveys escalation through category, while confidential remains a transport field.

A cutover and rollback record with the same normal and failure suites, exact identities, comparison thresholds, bounded canary scope, critical stop conditions, old-port SocketError.ConnectionRefused evidence, new-port receipt, actual three-case offline rollback rerun, retained prior adapter and serving bundle, and a statement that OFFLINE_ELIGIBLE is not deployment authorization.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Which behavior in your application would break even if both servers accept the same request path? Identify the owned field or event, classify it as required, transformed, rejected, or unavailable, name the evidence that would establish it, and specify the recovery or rollback action if it regresses.

cues.text: Separate the model runtime, inference server, gateway, application adapter, and public contract so each has one visible responsibility.
Draw five bounded layers and annotate identity, policy, protocol, model execution, and evidence ownership.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: A static five-row table maps the public contract, adapter, gateway, inference server, and runtime to responsibilities and forbidden responsibilities.

cues.text: Distinguish liveness, instance readiness, model readiness, and exact served-model identity across startup, pressure, update, and rollback.
Define inputs, outputs, streaming, errors, identity, authorization, limits, cancellation, retryability, telemetry, and overload before exposing traffic.
Ask whether a live process serving the wrong model should be marked ready.
Describe compatibility as a versioned tested subset with required, transformed, ignored, emulated, rejected, and unavailable behavior.
Compare baseline and candidate through the same conformance and evaluation suites, canary narrowly, and preserve tested rollback.

Begin at the repository root in PowerShell 7.6 or newer and keep this same session for the whole lab. The command captures the absolute repository root before entering the lab folder, which prevents later blocks from resolving a relative path underneath an already changed working directory. Explain the qualification boundary precisely: this lab was tested with PowerShell 7.6.6, .NET 10.0.12, and a normal Python 3.13.9 installation exposing python. The code is intended for Python 3.11 or newer, but other versions have not been qualified by the supplied evidence. The repository carries scripts and tests, not the runtime archive or model binary. Artifact identity comes from exact byte counts, hashes, pinned revisions, and full extracted-tree verification. The friendly alias p42-qwen3-06b does not prove those bytes. Ask learners to notice that the downloads total 657874317 bytes, while extracted DLLs and evidence require additional disk space. Memory and timing remain unknown until measured locally, so treat the CPU work as long-running and do not interpret the lesson estimate as an inference guarantee. Demonstrate the secret boundary carefully. RandomNumberGenerator fills a 32-byte array, the key enters only the current environment, and Start transfers it to the child as LLAMA_API_KEY. The same key remains available for the live client. Cleanup stops only a process whose state can be ownership checked, then removes and clears the key.

Separate three evidence streams before interpreting results. Synthetic unit tests challenge client behavior with offline HTTP fixtures. The live receipt observes requests against the local model service. Setup and lifecycle records establish artifact and process ownership facts. None can substitute for another. The qualifying receipt has 12 checks: nine named live observations and three not-observed entries for server-side cancellation, stop and restart recovery, and artifact hashes. Review each state rather than treating the file as one overall PASS. Public health is intentionally unauthenticated, missing-key rejection is tested separately, and the client receipt observes wrong-key rejection. For streaming, network chunks have no event meaning. The parser must buffer complete SSE records, collect textual deltas, and require terminal DONE. The 50 millisecond timeout is an experiment, not a universal fact. If a reply wins the race, record client_timeout as not-observed and fail that learner gate without declaring the server broken. Likewise, four successful concurrent responses are an overload sample, not a capacity or rate-limit guarantee. The independent lifecycle test uses a fresh secret held continuously across its two owned server cycles, then clears it only after the test's final stop. It does not start another baseline server. Correct the misconception that restart proof or hashes must be embedded in the port-only receipt. They are separate evidence.

Treat every failure label as a causal statement. A bad hash means the bytes are wrong. A full-tree mismatch means part of the runtime bundle changed. An occupied port means another owner exists. A stop refusal means recorded ownership no longer matches. None should be repaired by editing a manifest or killing a process by name. Then move to the streaming mutation. The commands use the saved absolute repository root and create a separate directory containing the client, unchanged protected tests, and an exclusive reference copy. Only the copied final missing-DONE guard is removed. The suite must fail, and the script extracts the exact protected test identifier so it can run that named test directly without guessing its class name. Explain why nonempty generated text is insufficient. A connection can end after partial text, and without terminal DONE the client cannot classify the stream as complete. Restore the module from the reference copy and require all eight tests to pass. Correct the misconception that this exercise should run against the live server. It should not. Mutation evidence establishes parser sensitivity; a fresh canonical-client receipt establishes live behavior.

State clearly that Adapter A and Adapter B are fictional offline mappings. They do not represent observations of two providers. Begin with the stable application fields, then trace each wire name through the completed matrix. Request and artifact identities must survive exactly. Category remains an allowed exact value. Explanation remains nonempty, although Adapter B performs the declared trimming transformation. Tools and confidential handling demonstrate why rejected and unavailable are useful classifications. Silently dropping either would create false compatibility. Explain the test accounting carefully. test_adapter_exercise.py contains seven original tests, test_adapter_rollback_boundaries.py adds five rollback-boundary tests, and those two files form the 12-test original regression. test_adapter_changed.py contributes five more methods, producing 17 tests across all three adapter files. test_conformance.py contains eight tests, producing 25 tests across all four files. The command verifies those counts from unittest output rather than claiming all 17 tests are in two older suites. Then check the exact six executable lines. The flawed candidate returns HOLD because it erases explanation, a user-visible outcome. Fixture latency, error, canary, and identity values are synthetic values from supplied code, not server measurements. OFFLINE_ELIGIBLE is not deployment authorization, and rollback must restore Adapter A and rerun all three original fixtures.

Present the changed requirement before showing the answer. Confidential recovery changes routing meaning, not merely request shape. The field must be a real Boolean, true is allowed only for account_recovery, and transport mapping must use confidential_account_recovery. The transport response carries the confidential flag, but the normalized application response remains exactly four fields. Its escalated category conveys the confidential routing result. Request identity and model-artifact identity remain exact, and original four-field cases must still work. Run the named original-failure test and explain its apparently surprising OK result. The test passes because it expects original Adapter B to raise ContractError. It does not claim that the original adapter implements confidential escalation. Learners then implement class ChangedAdapter with map_request and normalize_response in an independent file. The harness imports that learner class, binds adapter_answer.ChangedAdapter to it before importing the unchanged protected tests, and therefore executes the learner implementation rather than the reference class. The protected suite includes original preservation and 15 negative changed cases. A nonzero result remains visible, and learners rerun the same harness until it passes. Only after that attempt does the command display the answer and run the reference and 17-test adapter regression suites. Correct the misconception that transport acceptance establishes compatibility. A request can be accepted while a required explanation, identity, or routing distinction is lost.

The final rehearsal changes exactly one operational variable: the port. It uses the saved absolute repository root, checks for recorded state, and uses Stop only when that state exists. The old-port proof is intentionally strict. ConnectAsync.Wait can throw AggregateException when the task faults. Only an inner SocketException with SocketError.ConnectionRefused proves closure. A successful connection fails the exercise, while a timeout or any other network error is inconclusive and also fails. The client is always disposed, and the successful-connection assertion is not swallowed by a broad catch. A new random key is appropriate because this is a new server lifecycle, but Start and the changed-port client must share that one key. Require a new receipt rather than overwriting the baseline. Explain which facts stay stable: model and runtime pins, alias, context, thread count, GPU layers, and parallelism. Explain which facts change: listener URL, recorded port, process instance, and receipt path. Require the same nine named live checks, while handling the 50 millisecond timeout honestly. If the reply arrives first, record not-observed and fail the experiment without claiming universal server failure. Final Stop runs before secret cleanup. Correct the misconception that a new PID or alias alone proves restart. Artifact verification, process ownership, listener ownership, endpoint behavior, and final stop are separate linked records.
Guide the endpoint contract, adapter mappings, conformance cases, cutover thresholds, and rollback decision.
Begin the check after the learner can defend health, identity, compatibility, failure, and migration contracts.

questions.prompt: Which layer should translate a stable application schema to a runtime-specific protocol?
questions.explanation: The adapter contains protocol differences while application outcomes remain stable.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between liveness and readiness?
choices: Liveness asks whether the process should be restarted; readiness asks whether it should receive traffic
questions.explanation: The probes serve different control-plane decisions.

questions.prompt: What does an OpenAI-compatible label safely establish?
choices: Only the subset demonstrated by current documentation and conformance tests for the exact server configuration
questions.explanation: Compatibility is bounded by version, endpoints, fields, model, configuration, and tested behavior.

questions.prompt: How should unsupported request fields be handled?
choices: Reject or explicitly transform them according to the versioned contract
questions.explanation: Silent omission creates hidden behavioral differences and unsafe assumptions.

questions.prompt: Which case belongs in a conformance suite?
choices: Normal, boundary, invalid, unauthorized, streaming, timeout, overload, restart, and recovery behavior
questions.explanation: The suite must cover the application contract and important failures.

questions.prompt: What supports a safe runtime cutover?
choices: Reusing a friendly alias without telemetry
The same conformance and evaluation suites, bounded canary, exact identities, thresholds, and tested rollback
questions.explanation: A controlled comparison and retained rollback make the change reviewable and reversible.
